subject: anatomy
title: Pharyngeal arches, clefts, pouches and face development

steps.tx: The **pharyngeal arches** are paired bars of mesoderm and neural crest in the embryonic neck. Each arch has its own cartilage, muscle, cranial nerve and artery. Humans form arches I, II, III, IV and VI, because the fifth arch does not contribute structures. Arches I to III form structures above the larynx, while IV and VI form the larynx and trachea.
steps.say: The pharyngeal arches are paired bars of mesoderm and neural crest in the embryonic neck. Each arch has its own cartilage, muscle, cranial nerve and artery. Humans form arches one, two, three, four and six, because the fifth arch does not contribute structures. Arches one to three form structures above the larynx, while four and six form the larynx and trachea.

steps.tx: The **first arch** gives the mandible, malleus, incus and the muscles of mastication, along with the anterior belly of digastric, tensor tympani and tensor veli palatini. The **second arch** gives the stapes, styloid process, stylohyoid ligament and the posterior belly of digastric. Agenesis of the first arch can therefore cause conductive deafness through loss of the malleus and incus.

steps.tx: The **pharyngeal pouches** are endodermal outpockets and the **clefts** are ectodermal grooves between arches. The first pouch forms the middle ear cavity, Eustachian tube and mastoid antrum. The second pouch forms the palatine tonsil. The third pouch gives the inferior parathyroid and thymus. The fourth pouch gives the superior parathyroid and, through the ultimobranchial body, the calcitonin-secreting C-cells.

rows: Middle ear, Eustachian tube, mastoid antrum

steps.tx: In **DiGeorge syndrome** the third and fourth pouches fail to develop properly, so the thymus and parathyroids are small or absent. The infant has hypocalcaemia from low parathyroid hormone and a missing thymic shadow on chest x-ray. The tongue develops from the first arch for its anterior two-thirds and from the third and fourth arches for the posterior third. Anterior two-thirds sensation is from the lingual nerve.
